newsitem.title: USA: Prudential said streamling NY commoditiy operation.
newsitem.headline: Prudential said streamling NY commoditiy operation.

text.p: In a bid to streamline its business and cut expenses, Prudential Securities will close its floor operations at some New York commodity exchanges, Prudential floor traders said Friday.

The move will result in about 25 to 30 jobs being lost in the metals and softs products trading areas, but some staff are being added to its oil desk on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), Prudential traders who requested anonymity, said Friday.

A Prudential Securities spokeman would not comment on whether the company intended to layoff any floor traders, but maintained the company was "absolutely committed to keeping our presence on the floor."
The job cuts, which will take effect in about two weeks, were viewed as mainly a cost-cutting measure, one Prudential floor trader said.
"Their excuse is we are not making money," the trader said. "Operations is a customer service, it is not supposed to make money," he added.
In the past year, other investment firms such as Merrill Lynch and J. Aron, a division of Goldman, Sachs & Co, have moved to cut costs by scaling back floor operations.
"I think there is a trend to more closely scrutinize floor staffs," one industry source said. "People get tired of not making any money and are getting rid of their head count."
A separate back office Prudential employee said that while the company had made no official announcement, he had also heard the company was cutting some of its floor operations.

"We have not been told anything official at all," he said. "But talk is that they are streamlining, getting away from different clerks and just having one or two large floor brokers do the trading for the firm."

"We have been hearing they are closing their floor operations," another Prudential trader said. "We don't think they are getting out of the commodity business, but looking to modify how they do business."

Rumors Prudential planned to reduce its staff have been swirling around the New York commodity exchange floors, such as NYMEX's COMEX metals trading division and the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) for the past few days, industry sources said.
